# frzdynamo

Remote content delivery for desktop apps. `frzdynamo` fetches **notification**, **onboarding** and **payment** campaigns from your server, caches them on the user's machine, picks the one that applies to the current user, and hands your app a folder to render.

Update what your users see without shipping a new app build. If the server is down or nothing applies, you get `null` and show your built-in UI.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frzdynamo.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frzdynamo)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/frzdynamo.svg)](./LICENSE)

## Features

- Three content types: `notification`, `onboarding`, `payment`
- Offline-friendly: works from the local cache when the server is unreachable
- Version-based syncing: only re-downloads when your server's version changes
- Country, platform and time-window targeting
- Notification scheduling by frequency (per day) or exact timestamps
- Automatic cleanup of campaigns that were removed from the server
- Simple API: two pollers and one one-shot function

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer
- An ESM project (`import` syntax). From CommonJS, use `await import("frzdynamo")`.
- Windows, macOS or Linux

## Installation

```bash
npm install frzdynamo
```

## Quick start

```js
import { onBoarding, payment, notification } from "frzdynamo";

// Onboarding: check every 60 seconds, for up to 10 minutes
const stopOnboarding = onBoarding(60_000, 10 * 60_000, (error, dir, active) => {
  if (error) return console.error(error);

  if (active && dir) {
    openOnboardingWindow(dir);      // dir is a folder with the campaign's html/css/js/assets
  } else {
    openDefaultOnboarding();        // nothing to show, use your built-in UI
  }
});

// Payment: check every 60 seconds until you stop it
const stopPayment = payment(60_000, null, (error, dir, active) => {
  if (active && dir) openPaymentPage(dir);
  else openDefaultPaymentPage();
});

// Notification: one-shot check, call it whenever you want to see if one is due
const dir = await notification();
if (dir) showNotification(dir);

// Stop a poller at any time
stopOnboarding();
stopPayment();
```

## API

### `onBoarding(interval, tillTime, callback)`
### `payment(interval, tillTime, callback)`

Start a polling loop. Each cycle syncs content from the server (if it changed) and calls your callback with the result.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `interval` | `number` (ms) | Time between checks. Minimum `30000`. Must be smaller than `tillTime`. |
| `tillTime` | `number` (ms) or `null` | How long to keep polling. `null` means until you call the returned `stop()`. Minimum `30000`. |
| `callback` | `function` | Called after every check, see below. |

**Callback: `(error, dir, active)`**

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | `Error` or `null` | Set if the check failed. |
| `dir` | `string` or `null` | Absolute path to the campaign folder to render, or `null`. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` when `dir` is set and there is content to show. |

**Returns** a `stop()` function. Calling it ends the loop and invokes the callback one last time with `(null, null, false)`.

**Throws** a `TypeError` or `RangeError` if `interval`, `tillTime` or `callback` are invalid.

### `notification()`

```js
const dir = await notification(); // string | null
```

Syncs notification content if needed and returns the folder of the notification that should be shown **right now**, or `null`. Because notifications follow scheduling rules (see [Notification scheduling](#notification-scheduling)), `null` is a normal result. Call it on your own schedule, for example once a minute.

## Configuration

The package reads these from `process.env`:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `serverUrl` | `https://yourServer.com/api/v2` | Base URL of your content server |
| `DIRPATH` | OS app-data folder | Overrides where cached content is stored |

Set them before your app starts, or load a `.env` file yourself (for example with `dotenv`) before importing `frzdynamo`.

## Server contract

Your server must expose four JSON files:


<serverUrl>/jsons/notification.json
<serverUrl>/jsons/payment.json
<serverUrl>/jsons/onboarding.json
```


### `notification.json`, `payment.json`, `onboarding.json`

All three share the same structure:

```json
{
  "api-global-version": "1.4.0",
  "country": [
    {
      "location": "india",
      "payload": [
        [
          {
            "id": "diwali-2026",
            "platforms": ["windows", "macos"],
            "start_time": 1793000000,
            "end_time": 1793600000,
            "frequency": 2,
            "time_array": [1793100000, 1793200000],
            "html": ["https://cdn.example.com/diwali/index.html"],
            "css": ["https://cdn.example.com/diwali/style.css"],
            "js": ["https://cdn.example.com/diwali/app.js"],
            "assets": ["https://cdn.example.com/diwali/banner.png"]
          }
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "location": "world",
      "payload": [[]]
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `api-global-version` | Dotted version string. A higher value triggers a re-download. |
| `country[].location` | A country name (see [Country targeting](#country-targeting)) or `"world"` as the fallback. |
| `country[].payload` | An array of groups; each group is an array of campaigns. |
| `id` (or `name`) | Unique campaign key. Becomes the folder name. Use only letters, digits, `-` and `_`. |
| `platforms` | Any of `"windows"`, `"macos"`, `"linux"`. |
| `start_time` / `end_time` | Unix timestamps in seconds. Omit either for no limit. |
| `frequency` | Notifications only. How many times per 24 hours it may be shown. |
| `time_array` | Notifications only. Unix timestamps at which it should be shown. |
| `html`, `css`, `js`, `assets` | Arrays of **absolute `http(s)` URLs**. Other values are ignored. |

## How it works

1. **Fetch:** the client downloads `base.json` and the content JSON for the requested type.
2. **Compare:** it compares versions with the cached copy. If nothing changed, it keeps what it has.
3. **Download:** for changed content, it downloads the campaign files for the user's matched country into the local cache.
4. **Prune:** campaign folders that no longer appear in the server config are deleted.
5. **Select:** it returns the folder of one campaign that fits the user's country, platform and time window.

**Fallbacks**, in order: the server, then the last cached copy, then a JSON file bundled with the package, then `null`.

## Where files are stored

```
<app-data>/user-assets/
├── base.json
├── notification/
│   ├── notification.json
│   └── assets/<campaignId>/...
├── payment/
│   ├── payment.json
│   └── assets/<campaignId>/...
├── onboarding/
│   ├── onboarding.json
│   └── assets/<campaignId>/...
├── notification-frequency.json
└── notification-timearray-shown.json
```

`<app-data>` is:

| OS | Location |
|---|---|
| Windows | `%APPDATA%` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support` |
| Linux | `~/.local/share` |

Set `DIRPATH` to use a different root.

## Targeting

### Country targeting

Each entry in `country` has a `location`. The first entry that matches the user is used; if none match, the `"world"` entry is used.

Built-in country names: `usa` / `us`, `india` / `in`, `uk` / `united kingdom` / `gb`, `brazil` / `br`. Matching is based on the user's system timezone.

### Platform targeting

A campaign is only used when its `platforms` array contains the current platform: `windows`, `macos` or `linux`.

### Time windows

A campaign is only used when the current time is between `start_time` and `end_time` (when set).

## Notification scheduling

For each eligible notification (right country, platform and time window, assets downloaded):

- **`time_array`:** eligible for 60 seconds after each listed timestamp, once per timestamp.
- **`frequency`:** eligible when at least `86400 / frequency` seconds have passed since it was last shown.
- **Neither set:** always eligible.

If several are eligible, one is picked at random. The library remembers what it has shown in `notification-frequency.json` and `notification-timearray-shown.json`.

Call `notification()` at least once every 60 seconds if you use `time_array`, or the window can be missed.

## Security

This package downloads **HTML, CSS and JavaScript** from your server and gives your app a folder to load. Treat that content like code you ship:

- Serve everything over **HTTPS** from servers and CDNs you control.
- In Electron, render campaigns in a sandboxed `BrowserWindow` with `contextIsolation: true` and `nodeIntegration: false`.
- Campaign `id` values are used as folder names, and removed campaigns are deleted from disk. Keep ids to letters, digits, `-` and `_`.
